interest: This collection of docket sheets provides historians with a valuable high-level index and chronological overview of U.S. diplomatic and military intelligence gathering on Japanese aviation capabilities before and during World War II. It uniquely captures the inter-agency flow of intelligence among the State Department, War Department, Navy Department, Department of Justice, and the Coordinator of Information (COI), showing how officials pieced together data on Japanese air strength, fuel consumption, and raw material bottlenecks from diverse global listening posts such as Havana, Dairen, Chungking, Berlin, and London. Of particular historical significance are the early intelligence reports on the Mitsubishi Zero fighter (initially identified as the 'Centenary Pursuit Plane') in late 1940, diplomatic tracking of German-Japanese negotiations over aircraft-for-raw-materials barter during Matsuoka's 1941 Berlin mission, and pre-war scrutiny of American aviation corporate contacts in Latin America attempting to bypass export controls.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's docket sheets ('List of Papers') for decimal file 894.248, covering internal and diplomatic records regarding Japanese aircraft, aviation equipment, production, and air strength between 1940 and 1944. Consisting of Form DS-46 and subsequent purport sheets (Sheets #6 and #7), the documents catalogue and summarize sub-files 34 through 52, tracing pre-war and wartime intelligence. Key subjects include attempted exports of American aviation equipment and aircraft to Japan (including an alleged Curtiss-Wright sales effort via Havana), intelligence on Japanese combat operations and losses in China, specifications of the Mitsubishi Zero ('Centenary Pursuit Plane type zero'), estimates of aircraft manufacturing capacity and raw material constraints (such as tin and aluminum), Axis technical cooperation and aircraft procurement discussions during Foreign Minister Matsuoka's visit to Berlin, fuel requirements estimated by Standard-Vacuum Oil, and Allied assessments of front-line Japanese air strength. Most listed records include cross-reference citations directing researchers to related decimal files on the European and Pacific wars.

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet (Form DS-46) recording file entries 34 and 35 regarding proposed and compliance-related exports of aviation equipment and airplanes to Japan in early 1940.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet, recorded on Form DS-46 and dated October 12, 1945, indexes entries 34 and 35 for decimal file 894.248. Entry 34 records information from Eclipse Aviation in Bendix, New Jersey, regarding aviation equipment shipments to Japan furnished in compliance with President Roosevelt's request and cross-referenced to the European War file series. Entry 35 details a War Department report concerning George Burris, an alleged representative of the Curtiss-Wright Company in Havana offering airplanes to Japanese officials, and the Japanese Navy Department's subsequent interest in procuring equipment.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Decimal File 894.248 (Sub-numbers 34-35)

subfiles.about: State Department purport sheet listing intelligence reports and correspondence on Japanese air operations, aircraft production, and foreign procurement from May 1940 to April 1942.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Sheet #6) catalogues entries 36 through 48 1/2, documenting diplomatic and military intelligence on Japanese aviation preceding and following the outbreak of the Pacific War. Notable items include Military Attaché reports on Japanese Army Air Forces and combat losses in China, investigation into Curtiss-Wright salesman George Burrus in the Caribbean, early Navy Department data on the Type Zero pursuit plane from Chungking, Justice Department memoranda on Japanese aluminum and aircraft manufacturing, and German-Japanese aircraft acquisition talks during Matsuoka's visit to Berlin. It also records aviation fuel estimates by Standard-Vacuum Oil, aircraft transshipment through Dairen, Soviet estimates of German plane deliveries, and a Coordinator of Information analysis of tin supplies in relation to airplane production.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Decimal File 894.248, Sheet #6 (Sub-numbers 36-48 1/2)

subfiles.about: State Department purport sheet indexing intelligence reports, export valuations, and Allied assessments of Japanese air strength from July 1942 to March 1944.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Page 7) lists entries 49 through 52 relating to Japanese aviation during the height of World War II. It details Justice Department reports on design improvements in the 'new style Zero,' statistical data on pre-war arms and munitions export licenses provided to Senator Scott W. Lucas, and British Embassy transmissions regarding Japanese air strength, including a Manchester Guardian article by Emil Speyer and a memorandum by Colonel Vickers. Later entries summarize War Department estimates of front-line Japanese aircraft and a March 1944 Chungking despatch analyzing Japan's overall aircraft position.
